atoms.sound: Hello everyone. Today, I'm going to talk about my family's story and how my grandparents migrated from Vietnam to Germany. First, I want to tell you why people left Vietnam at the time my grandparents decided to leave as well. Some people came to Germany to work as guest workers as there were labour shortages. Others left Vietnam because they wanted to study abroad. Lastly, people from South Vietnam fled the country because of war.

My grandparents lived in a small village in Vietnam. One day, they decided to change their lives. The country suffered from political instability and economic problems. That's why my grandparents decided to leave and start a new life abroad in Germany. They were hoping for a better and more stable future.

Before my grandparents could leave the country, they first had to travel to a coastal town by foot. They only took as many things with them as they could carry. They left most of their belongings in Vietnam. Once they reached the coastal town, they were able to board an overcrowded boat. Lots of people wanted to leave the country, so there wasn't much space. My grandmother told me that she was scared that the boat might sink. Luckily, they arrived in Europe safely.

One of the biggest questions remaining is: How to feel home away from home? I asked my grandparents how they managed to not feel homesick so much, and they said that there were three major things that helped them a lot. The first thing is cooking familiar meals. For them, it's fresh spring rolls and Bahn Mieh. The second thing is decorating their home with items that remind them of Vietnam. Over the years, my grandparents collected several traditional lanterns that they hung up at home. Lastly, it helped them to celebrate cultural festivities like the Moon Festival or Vietnamese New Year. Those festivities usually bring the whole neighbourhood together.
